mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the federal funds rate by more than 0.25% within the last month signals a loosening of monetary policy, which typically leads to increased liquidity in the markets and positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 20d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the signal, or the correlation between FEDFUNDS decreases and SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: An increase in the unemployment rate by more than 0.5% over the last two months indicates weakening labor market conditions, which historically precedes negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 60d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the signal, or the correlation between UNRATE increases and SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in housing starts (HOUST) by more than 5% over the last two months signals a strengthening demand in the housing market, which is a leading indicator of economic growth and positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 20d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the signal, or the correlation between HOUST increases and SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 1% over the last two months indicates a contraction in supply, which can lead to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as companies face increased costs and reduced output.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 60d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the signal, or the correlation between INDPRO decreases and SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: An always-on signal where a low federal funds rate (below 1%) suggests a sustained accommodative monetary policy, which typically supports positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 5d returns in > 60% of instances with FEDFUNDS < 1%, or the correlation between low FEDFUNDS and SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: An interaction-driven signal where a simultaneous increase in real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) and a decrease in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) over the last month indicates strengthening consumer demand and labor market conditions, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS increase & UNRATE decrease in 1 month
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 20d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the signal, or the joint effect of RSAFS and UNRATE changes on SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A regime-conditional signal where an increase in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) by more than 200,000 over the last month, during a period of low unemployment (UNRATE < 5%), signals a tightening labor market, which can lead to wage inflation and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 60d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the signal, or the interaction effect of PAYEMS increase and low UNRATE on SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A regime-conditional signal where a rapid increase in the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) by more than 0.5% in a single month, during a period of already high inflation (CPIAUCSL > 2.5% YoY), signals an acceleration of inflationary pressures, which can lead to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as the market anticipates monetary tightening.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL increase > 0.5% in 1 month & CPIAUCSL > 2.5% YoY
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the signal, or the correlation between rapid CPIAUCSL increases and SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).
